overview: The micro:bit was designed for classrooms first, hardware hobbyists second — it ships with a 5x5 LED matrix, two buttons, a compass, an accelerometer, and (on v2) a speaker and microphone all built in, so a first project needs zero extra components. Instead of pin headers, it has a distinctive gold-plated edge connector: five large ring pads (for easy crocodile-clip or banana-plug connections) plus 20 smaller contacts for more advanced breakout boards. It's usually programmed visually (MakeCode blocks) or in Python before students graduate to C++/Arduino-style boards.
simpleSummary: A classroom-friendly microcontroller that already has lights, buttons, and sensors built in.

specifications.microcontroller: Nordic nRF52833, Arm Cortex-M4 with FPU, 64 MHz
specifications.builtInSensors: Accelerometer, compass, microphone, light/temperature sensing via the LED matrix
specifications.connector: Micro-USB, plus a JST 2xAAA battery connector

pinMap.name: P3
pinMap.function: Edge pin; general-purpose I/O, also drives an LED matrix column internally.
pinMap.gotcha: Using this pin for external wiring while the LED display is active can cause visible flicker or unexpected LED states.

pinMap.function: Large ring pad; regulated 3V output for external sensors/actuators.

pinMap.function: Large ring pad; common ground reference.

useCases.title: First programmable device for a classroom
useCases.scenario: Use MakeCode's block editor to scroll text, react to shake gestures, or play simple games on the LED matrix — no extra hardware needed.

useCases.title: Crocodile-clip physical computing
useCases.scenario: Clip wires directly to the P0/P1/P2/3V/GND ring pads to build simple circuits (e.g. a banana keyboard) with no soldering.

useCases.title: Bluetooth-connected wearable
useCases.scenario: Use the built-in BLE radio to send accelerometer data to a phone app.

useCases.title: External sensor breakout via edge connector
useCases.scenario: Mount on a breakout board to access all 25 edge pins for I2C sensors or multiple servos.

oftenConfusedWith: Arduino Uno (text-based C++ only, no built-in sensors/display)
oftenUpgradedTo: Raspberry Pi Pico (more raw I/O, no built-in sensors/display)
